title: Balance a production line
summary: Split a line into one function block per machine, and send alternate blanks to each so that both machines make four products.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Move the control of one machine into a function block and use one instance for each machine.
Give two machines of different speeds the same control, so that each finishes four cycles.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ProductionLine.st machine A is controlled by statements written in the program itself, and machine B has no control at all. Make both machines work the same way, with the control written only once, and light Green when both have finished four cycles.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what is written once for both machines, and what each machine keeps for itself.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, count the blanks: eight arrive, one every six seconds, and the arm sends every second one to machine B; machine A needs 3 s per cycle and machine B 6 s, so each makes four.
stages.checkpoint: A machine starts a cycle only when it reports one blank at rest, and a Start at any other moment is a misfire: misfires stays at zero.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting project controls only machine A, so machine B never gets a blank into its chamber, no base is made and Green never lights. Give machine B the same control without writing it a second time, and light Green when both machines have finished four cycles.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named balanced-production-line and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch both machines in the 3D view and read produced: and misfires: in the facts text.
stages.checkpoint: Machine A makes a lid and machine B a base on each cycle, and misfires stays at zero.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The EVENTUALLY assertion proves both machines made a product and both bins received one; the ALWAYS assertion proves no Start was a misfire and nothing fell.
stages.checkpoint: The grade cannot count the products: it reads Green, which the program lights from its own count, so read produced: in the facts for the real number.

hints.text: Look at the variables that only machine A's control uses, and ask which of them machine B would need its own copy of. A function block keeps a separate copy of its variables in every instance.

Write a function block, for example Cell, that keeps its own Step, its Travel and Eject timers and its Cycles count, so that two instances never share them. Move into it the statements of machine A, from StartA := FALSE; to the FeedA line, renaming StepA, TravelA, EjectA and CyclesA to Step, Travel, Eject and Cycles, and EyeA, ReadyA, DoneA, FeedA and StartA to Seen, Ready, Done, Feed and Start, and delete them and those variables from the program. Pass Active, Seen, Ready and Done in and take Feed, Start and Cycles out. Set Start to FALSE at the top so that it lasts one scan, and call each instance once per scan. In the program, declare MachA : Cell and MachB : Cell, call them with Active := Active, Seen := EyeA and EyeB, Ready := ReadyA and ReadyB, Done := DoneA and DoneB, copy Feed and Start to FeedA, StartA, FeedB and StartB, and light Green when both Cycles are at least 4.

faultCases: The starting project controls only machine A, so machine B never gets a blank into its chamber, no base is made and Green never lights.
